prompt:
High-fidelity mobile UI design comp: one portrait phone screen filling the frame.

The app is Squirrel, a personal memory aid. This is its record surface — where everything said and done is kept, and where you talk to Buddy. Same world as a rail concourse departure board: brushed steel chassis, matte black flap cells. But this screen pairs a small live board at the top with a continuous printed paper log below, because a log is append-only the way a teleprinter roll is: nothing can be un-printed.

STRUCTURE, top to bottom:
1. A slim brushed steel header rail carrying a CAST BRASS HERALDIC CREST at the far left, riveted to the steel: a squirrel in profile with a full curled tail, raised polished brass relief inside a small shield the height of the rail, worn and slightly tarnished at its edges. Beside it in tiny wide-tracked uppercase monospace "SQUIRREL", and at the right "THE LOG".
2. A SHORT LIVE BOARD, about one fifth of the height: two matte black flap rows showing what has just arrived. Row one: cream monospace time "09:12", then in condensed uppercase white paint on flap cells "THE BOILER NOISE", then tiny cream monospace at the right "KEPT". Row two: "14:02", "WATER THE PLANTS", and at the right in green monospace "DONE".
3. A hard horizontal seam: the steel chassis gives way to a PAPER ROLL that emerges from a slot and runs to the bottom edge of the screen. The paper is warm off-white (#f4ece0) with a faint horizontal fibre texture, a torn deckle along the slot edge, and fine sprocket-hole perforations down both margins.
4. THE LOG, printed on that paper in dark grey-black dot-matrix monospace, a continuous run of timestamped lines down the screen. Each line begins with a small time in lighter grey, then a short uppercase role tag, then the text. Render these lines exactly:
   09:12  CAPTURED   the boiler makes a noise when the heating comes on
   09:12  CONTROL    Kept.
   11:40  YOU        i can't start any of this
   11:40  CONTROL    Which of these is it?
   11:41  YOU        too big
   11:41  CONTROL    Forget the rest of it. Just do the smallest piece you can see.
   14:02  DID        water the plants
   Every CONTROL line carries, in its left margin just before the timestamp, a SMALL INKED RUBBER STAMP of a squirrel in profile with a curled tail — about the height of two text lines, stamped in warm orange-brown ink (#b3541e), each impression slightly rotated and unevenly inked so no two are identical. Only the CONTROL lines carry it; the YOU, CAPTURED and DID lines have an empty margin. The CONTROL lines also sit in slightly heavier ink. The final "DID" line carries a rubber-stamped orange (#e66d0d) circular STAMP over its right end reading "DONE", slightly rotated and imperfectly inked.
5. Beneath the "Which of these is it?" line, four small answer chips rendered as tiny matte black flap cells with cream uppercase monospace: TOO BIG, BORING, DON'T KNOW HOW, NOT TODAY.
6. At the very foot, a brushed steel slot with a fresh paper edge showing, and a tiny wide-tracked monospace prompt on it: "TYPE TO ADD A LINE".

MATERIALS: brushed steel chassis, matte black flaps, warm printed paper with sprocket margins, dot-matrix ink, one rubber stamp.
STRICT PALETTE: #17130d #0c0a07 #f4ece0 #d8cec0 #2a2620 #fed6a7 #e66d0d #529414.
TYPE: condensed uppercase sans on the flap cells; dot-matrix monospace for every printed log line; tiny wide-tracked uppercase monospace for rails and tags.
MOOD: a signal-box log book that cannot be edited. Mechanical, warm, permanent. The board above is what is true now; the paper below is what happened and is never rewritten.
